title: Who Is Actually Following Up? Mapping the MIRI Governance Pivot Across the AI Safety Org Landscape

original_idea.body:
# Who Is Actually Following Up? Mapping the MIRI Governance Pivot Across the AI Safety Org Landscape

**Problem:** A flagged surprising result is MIRI's 2025 pivot from pure alignment to governance, implying a belief that technical alignment alone is insufficient. Whether this is an isolated move or part of a broader, measurable shift of technical-safety organizations toward governance has not been characterized.

**Direction:** Characterize the pivot pattern. Build a sample of ~20-30 AI safety organizations/labs and, using public output (publication lists, blog archives, job postings, mission statements over time), code each org's research-vs-governance emphasis at two time points (e.g. 2022 vs 2025). Measure the aggregate drift and identify which orgs moved most toward governance. Use a transparent keyword/LLM classifier with hand-validated labels.

**Why it matters:** If technically-focused orgs are systematically reallocating toward governance, it is a strong field-level signal about perceived tractability of alignment — directly relevant to research-prioritization and funding policy. Entirely public data, no compute-heavy work, and exactly the meta-analysis individual labs are too inside-view to do.

**Relevant context:** Context file surprising result: MIRI 2025 governance agenda pivot, with explicit suggested follow-up to analyze whether other technical orgs are pivoting similarly.
